title: ALMA Observations Show Major Mergers Among the Host Galaxies of Fast-growing, High-redshift Supermassive Black Holes
question: Are major mergers important drivers of rapid early SMBH growth, as tested with ALMA continuum and [C II] observations of six z≃4.8 quasar hosts, three FIR-bright and three FIR-faint?

data.angular_resolution: ~0.3 arcsec at 330 GHz (~2 kpc); beams 0.38-0.54 x 0.29-0.31 arcsec

what.value: Mg II-based redshifts, BH masses and bolometric luminosities

evidence.quote: b Mg II λ 2798-based redshifts taken from T11.
a SDSS-based redshifts taken from Hewett & Wild (2010).
For all three FIR-faint systems (bottom row), we adopted the measurements of the stacked Herschel signal (N14).
The compilation, adapted from Cicone et al. (2015), includes inactive star forming galaxies at low and intermediate redshifts
a sample of z ≃ 0 elliptical galaxies (taken from Kormendy & Ho 2013, black circles)

recipe.method: Observatory scripts for visibilities, then CLEAN with Briggs robust 0.5; continuum from two upper windows; uv continuum subtraction for [C II] from the lower two

recipe.goal: Measure sizes, line fluxes, widths and redshifts
recipe.method: 2D Gaussian fits to continuum and moment-0 images; 1D spectra from Gaussian-based apertures (1.5-2 sigma) fitted with a single Gaussian; the spatial fluxes adopted

recipe.goal: Derive FIR luminosities, TIR and SFR
recipe.method: Gray-body SED (Td=47 K, beta=1.6) and Chary & Elbaz 2001 templates anchored to ALMA continuum; SFR = L_TIR(8-1000 µm)/10^10 Lsun
key_parameters: L_FIR integrated over 42.5-122.5 µm; TIR over 8-1000 µm
assumptions: AGN contribution to FIR neglected (<~10%); Chabrier IMF

recipe.method: M_dyn = 9.8e8 (D_[CII]/kpc)(FWHM/100 km/s)^2 / sin^2(i) Msun, with cos(i) = a_min/a_maj; dust mass from optically thin dust; gas mass via gas-to-dust 100
assumptions: Inclined rotating disk, v_circ = 0.75 FWHM/sin i; Td=47 K, beta=1.6; gas-to-dust 100

recipe.goal: Compare with SF main sequence and BH-host relations; assess mergers
recipe.method: Compare SFR vs M_dyn with the main-sequence relation; BH growth rate from L_bol with eta=0.1; compare M_BH/M_dyn with local ellipticals; identify companions via continuum and [C II] redshift
software: MATLAB package for astronomy and astrophysics
assumptions: Host mass grows only via star formation at CE01-based SFR

evidence.quote: separated by ∼ 14 − 45kpc and < 450kms −1 from the quasar hosts
the L [C II ] /L FIR ratio is in the range of (2.1 − 9.4) × 10 −4
span a wide range of ∼ 260 − 3040 M ⊙ yr −1 for the gray-body SEDs
The dust masses we derive are in the range M dust ∼ (0.4 − 4.8) × 10 8 M ⊙ for the quasar hosts
we obtain dynamical masses of M dyn ≃ (3.7 − 7.5) × 10 10 M ⊙ for the quasar hosts
which are in the range M BH /M dyn ∼ 1/260 − 1/10

not_stated_but_needed: CLEAN parameters: deconvolver, threshold, masks, iterations, image size
Line-free channels and exact spectral windows used for continuum subtraction
Flux calibrator and flux scale uncertainty
Whether pipeline or manual calibration scripts were used and which pipeline version
Aperture and fitting details for the 2D Gaussian fits
How inclinations were bounded for unresolved sources
missing_for_reproduction: Herschel and T11 data tables from other papers
score_reason: Data are public and the main steps are described, but CLEAN settings and flux calibration are missing, and some inputs come from earlier papers.
rediscovery_reason: Data are public, the recipe is mostly clear, and the main results (fluxes, FWHM, SFR, M_dyn) are numeric.
